--- title: "[score_cr()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Bundled competing-risks evaluation: concordance, Brier, and integrated Brier. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_metrics.py#L2295-L2430){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python score_cr( surv, incidence_prob, *, data=None, cause, times, tau=None, conf_level=0.95, format=None ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Computes the main prediction-performance metrics for a cause-specific cumulative incidence model in one call, returning a tidy summary frame. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [surv]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Surv | Outcome | str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A multistate `Surv` response. An `Outcome` or a formula response such as `'Surv(time, status == 2)'` is also accepted, with its columns read from `data`. [incidence_prob]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Predicted CIF for the cause of interest, shape `(n_subjects, n_times)`. [cause]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Integer cause code. [times]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Evaluation times (1-D array-like), matching the columns of `incidence_prob`. [tau]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Truncation time for the concordance index. Defaults to the last value in `times`. [conf_level]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.95]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Confidence level for the concordance CI. [format]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : DataFrame backend for the returned table. [data]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A data frame (pandas, Polars, PyArrow, DuckDB, a lazy frame, ...) holding the columns named by the response and `incidence_prob`. When `surv` is an `Outcome` or a formula, rows with a missing value in any column used are dropped first, along with the matching rows of any arrays passed alongside. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [DataFrame]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : One row per metric with columns `metric`, `estimate`, and (for the concordance) `se`, `conf_low`, `conf_high`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#611a7cbd .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw import numpy as np mg = gw.load_dataset("mgus2", backend="polars") etime = np.where(mg["pstat"] == 1, mg["ptime"], mg["futime"]) event = np.where(mg["pstat"] == 1, 1, 2 * mg["death"]) y = gw.Surv.multistate(time=etime, event=event, states=("pcm", "death")) fg = gw.FineGray(cause="pcm").fit(y, covariates=["age", "sex"], data=mg) eval_times = np.array([120, 240, 360]) cif_pred = fg.predict_cumulative_incidence( mg, times=eval_times, format="pandas" ).drop(columns="time").values.T gw.score_cr(y, incidence_prob=cif_pred, cause=1, times=eval_times, format="polars") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}
